question: can every numeric claim in the manuscript body be shown to come from a receipt

first_attempt.method: a loose matcher compared each manuscript number against all 396 numeric values in the experiment receipts, allowing a factor of one hundred either way and rounding to the stated precision
first_attempt.apparent_result: 66 of 66 body numbers matched, zero unbound
first_attempt.validity_test: random numbers of the same shape were fed to the same matcher
first_attempt.reason: a matcher that accepts 82.5 percent of random numbers cannot establish provenance; the apparent perfect score is mostly the test being permissive, which is the same defect class as the cue-coverage endpoint falsified earlier at a false-positive rate of 0.969

adopted.method: explicit two-sided binding: each bound number names a receipt and a path, the rendered form must appear in the body, and the receipt must still hold the bound value

failing_first_tests.mutation: change the reported task share in the prose only
change the value in the receipt only
failing_first_tests.message: receipt value 25.0 no longer matches the bound number

adopted.note: both directions fire, so prose and receipt cannot drift apart independently

honest_limit: fifteen checks bind the headline numbers; the remaining body numbers are not individually bound, so this is a partial guarantee and is reported as such

rejected_bindings.reason: the variance-block receipt stores an episode list, not a count, so the path resolved to a list; rebound to the re-derivation receipt which records the count
no receipt field holds this value, and binding it to a nearby number with a wide tolerance would have made the check meaningless; left unbound instead
